name: Hobble corset

card.summary: A long corset dress or longline corset covering the thighs or legs, worn to create a narrow-hipped, smooth silhouette and an upright carriage.
card.note: Restricts stride, sitting and stairs; long-term corset wear is linked to weakened core muscles.

quick.overview:
A hobble corset is a corset long enough to cover the legs partly or fully, named for its similarity to the hobble skirt. It shapes the torso and legs into a smooth, narrow line and holds the wearer upright, which is the appearance payoff: a sleek silhouette and straight posture while worn.

It was part of the 1908 to 1914 narrow-skirted fashion. Today it appears in costume and corset-dress wear; studies of corsets in general describe breathing and comfort effects.
quick.how: It is worn as an outer or under-garment dress-length corset that is laced or fastened closed. Stiff boning makes stairs and sitting difficult.
quick.risks: Stride, sitting and stairs are restricted. Corsets in general reduced lung capacity in measured studies, and long-term wear can weaken core and back muscles.

lead: A hobble corset, also called a corset dress, is a long corset that covers the legs partly or fully and produces effects similar to those of a hobble skirt [1]. It gives a smooth, narrow shape from torso to legs and an upright stance while worn.

From 1908 to 1914 the fashionable narrow-hipped, narrow-skirted silhouette led to longer corsets covering the thighs; longline corsets made the waist look higher and the hips narrower [1]. The style faded during World War I, partly to save materials, and evolved into the elasticated girdle [1].

chain: Long boned corset compresses torso and hips
Smooth narrow line from waist to legs
angle.text: The garment reshapes the figure while worn, narrowing the hips and creating a smooth, upright line. Wearers choose it for the dramatic silhouette it produces.

infobox: Restricts stride; stairs and sitting harder [1]

paras: The hobble skirt had a hem narrow enough to impede the wearer's stride and peaked between 1908 and 1914 [2]. Wearers sometimes tied their legs at the knee to keep skirts from splitting [2]. Corsets lengthened to suit the line, and contemporaries found them uncomfortable and cumbersome, adding elastic strips [1]. The skirt faded at the outbreak of World War I [2].

Corsets were believed to ensure good posture and a smooth torso, and an upright military bearing was a reason to wear them [1]. Long-term wear can weaken core and back muscles, which may relieve back pain briefly but can lead to reliance and more lower-back pain [1].

No studies found on hobble corsets specifically. Studies of moderately laced corsets generally found reduced lung capacity of 2% to 29% (average 9%) and more breathlessness during moderate exercise [1].
Stiff boning can make stairs hard to climb and sitting difficult [1]. Hobble skirts were associated with accidents, including reported deaths in 1910 and 1911 [2].

timeline.event: Hobble-skirt silhouette emerges and begins its peak [2].
Longline corsets abandoned around World War I, later evolving into elasticated girdles [1][2].
